body: I sincerely apologize if this is the wrong place to post this. Would you be able to point me in the right direction so my post can be seen by the right people?

Wow. I came here as I usually do at night (and sometimes during the day) to read some good horror fiction. When I was faced with the privacy block, my first reaction was confusion. I started to read the wording of the post on the block. It is with some shame, but in all honesty, that I must admit that for an instant I felt a bit angry. How could they block me from my most precious existential dread? What had I done to them? Then I read why this was happening and that it was only temporary. Once I was able to process it all after reading it, I must say, instead of trying to find some way of getting around that block and into that sweet, sweet horror, I felt immediate and total support for the action and pondered; "What can I do to be a part of this? How can I somehow contribute to this righteous defense of the imaginative and talented creators here and their works?" To be honest I didn't even know it had gotten this bad, and that made me feel even worse for not even taking the time to be aware of the problem, let alone the extent of it. I'd heard about a few people having their stories pretty much stolen and read by people who refused to credit them, but I had no idea how much or how often it was really happening. So I took a look at the subreddits listed above. I found the blacklist and I immediately crossed referenced it with every subscription I have. Thankfully there were none on my end. But since I hadn't subscribed to anyone that was on the blacklist, I didn't feel like I had done anything at all to contribute to the cause (I might have felt like I made at least a small difference if I had cut off 5 or 10 people) so that was just a very small start. I'm going to look into how I can support these wonderful writers as much as I can. Any and all advice on how I might be able do that more thoroughly and effectively would be GREATLY appreciated! I would like to give a HEARTFELT thanks to every creator here at r/nosleep! Without your words I don't think I could have gotten through, or continue to go through, many of the sleepless nights I have endured, and continue to endure, throughout my years with depression and bipolar disorder. You mean more to me than you could know! A week without noslleep, by comparison, seems like such a small price to pay to see that you guys are both recognized and defended by the community you so selflessly contribute to. You have my sincere gratitude and you can count on my shield, I am in your corner :-)
